Option 1: "که شادی و غم گیتی نمی کنند دوام - ز غم مباش غمین و مشو از شادی شاد"
First line: "That joy and sorrow of the world do not endure" (they are not lasting). Second line: "Do not be sad because of sorrow, and do not become happy because of joy." Actually "از شادی شاد" maybe "be happy from joy"? The message: impermanence, don't be attached to sorrow or joy.

Option 2: "به نیک و بد برآید زندگانی - نماند شادی و غم جاودانی"
Translation: "Life comes with good and bad; happiness and sorrow do not remain eternal." So similar: life includes both, nothing permanent.

Option 3: "بر سر اوالد آدم هر چه آید بگذرد - گوش کن پند ای پسر از بهر دنیا غم مخور"
First line: "On the head of Adam's offspring, whatever comes passes." Means everything passes. Second line: "Listen to advice, O son, for the world, do not worry about sorrow." So also about transience, advice not to worry.

Option 4: "کاروان طبع طرب و شادی از آن کم گذرد - بس که روز و شبم از دل سپه غم گذر"
First line: "The caravan of nature (or temperament) of joy and happiness passes little." Not sure. "کاروان طرب و شادی از آن کم گذرد" maybe "the caravan of merriment and joy passes rarely." Second line: "Enough that my day and night from the heart of the army of sorrow pass." Hard to parse. Might be about sorrow dominating day/night, maybe more about sorrow overwhelming.
